doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Black Hawk Sunday sessions and visiting players
summary: Cal Tjader joins; Mel Lewis, Tal Farlow and others sit in on Sundays.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I don’t know what her problem was. We also — who else did we back? I’m just trying to think of who the heck else. Well Cal Tjader, he joined us for a while of course, and then for a while he had a trio at the Black Hawk so we had the two trios for a while and then when things started to get shaky and they cut his two men out and he played with us because Jerome left and Pony left. Pony left first, he went with Lionel Hampton. But he didn’t last very long. Then Jerome went with Hamp and he eventually came back. But for a while there was just Vernon and Cal and Richard Wyands and I. And I’m just trying to think of who the heck — people would come sit in, see on Sundays we’d have a Sunday jam session. And people would come sit in. Now Howard Dedunne, Ed Thigpen, I guess that was during the Korean War, they were at Ft. Ord, they used to come up and sit in with us on Sundays. One Sunday Mel Lewis, he was with the Ray Anthony band, and they were playing the St. Francis Hotel. He came over and sat in with us, he and the bass player, I think his last name is — I remember he and the bass player, they both came over. He sat in with us. Tal Farlow, he was there with Red Norvo, and Red Mitchell. Mingus had been with them but he had left so Ray Mitchell. So Tal Farlow, he came in on a Sunday and sat in with us. Oh he played, oh what a good player. Then the Four Freshmen were at Thacks at one time, and Bob Flanigan, trombonist, he came in and sat in with us. And oh my God who else. Oh Jeez.
Well you’ve just about done it all.
